verdicts.note: One explicit statement on his own site, checked against the cached page: working families and small businesses carry 'a disproportionate share of the tax burden while billion-dollar corporations find ways to avoid paying theirs' [S2]. The statement is about who pays rather than about new revenue, and he takes no position on ESSB 6346 or I-645, so +1 at medium is the ceiling.

There is no statement of his own, so the score rests only on endorsements. Two separate reproductive-rights PACs (Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates and Pro-Choice Washington, both confirmed on the cached endorsements page [S4]) meet the minimum for the guide's 'strong endorsement pattern' that medium requires. This differs from the single-PPAA-endorsement cases that other refutations downgraded. Magnitude 1 is right because nothing on gender identity or sports is recorded. If a second reviewer reads 'strong pattern' as needing more than two topical endorsers, low would be the fallback.

The lone-ESSB-6346 rule does not bind here. Besides the no vote on 6346 [S3], the dossier has three independent recorded no votes on 2025 revenue bills (ESSB 5813, ESSB 5814, ESHB 2081; checked in the cached roll calls) [S5][S6][S7]. It also has his sponsored amendment 2591, whose EFFECT clause expires all ESSB 5814 services taxes on July 1, 2026 [S4], his 2025 amendment 1333 to ESHB 2081 [S7], and the campaign-site plank 'by cutting taxes' [S16]. Even setting aside 2591 because it was offered to the same bill, -2/high stands.

Two recorded no votes on the 2025-27 operating budget [S8] and the 'results problem' / 'past $80 billion' critique of the 2026 supplemental [S15] support high. Holding the score at -1 rather than -2 reflects that the same update faults the majority for cutting education by $1 billion [S15].

The cached roll calls confirm no on EHB 1217 House passage (53-42) and on the conference report (54-44) [S9]. Not in the dossier: he also voted yes on the failed motion to concur in the Senate amendments (48-50), probably in favor of the Senate's narrower version. That does not change the direction. Medium is right because the pamphlet's 'practical solutions to expand affordable housing' [S1] has no direction.

'Fully funding the police department' and the fentanyl plank are verified on the cached campaign home page [S16], and the pamphlet backs law enforcement [S1]. The site's text dates from his first campaign, so medium, not high, is correct.

The axis applies to State contests. He voted no on ESHB 1296 House passage and concurrence [S11], and yes on ten failed Republican floor amendments to it (in the cached roll call). The bill revised the I-2081 parental rights [S12]. That is one bill with no I-1 statement, so -1 at medium rather than ±2/high.
